The U.S. House on Tuesday voted, 370-48, in favor of a stopgap spending measure that is expected to avert a government shutdown this fall ahead of the 2026 midterm election, despite objections from GOP hard-liners.

The legislation, which the Senate passed in August before breaking for its summer recess, would keep the government funded through Dec. 11.

The measure now heads to President Donald Trump's desk for his signature.
